title: Briefing: Italy's student and cost-of-living protests, France's high school protests and Albania's student protests
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Friday, October twenty-third. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.

The security decree is published as Decree-Law number 190 of 2026 in Gazzetta Ufficiale number 246 on October twenty-second and takes effect October twenty-third, Il Sole 24 Ore and Scuola Informa report. That's confirmed by independent reports. What's next: a reconciled national total for arrests and injuries over October sixteenth to eighteenth.

Prime Minister Lecornu receives the mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon at Matignon on Thursday as they had requested after the October seventeenth violence; the mayors had asked for a precise, transparent account of how that day's events unfolded. That's confirmed by independent reports. We're watching what concrete steps follow the October twenty-second meeting between Lecornu and the mayors.

A Tirana court rules that 18 arrests from the protests were unlawful and orders the release of 27 people, rejecting prosecutors' requests to impose security measures on them; nine others are ordered to report periodically to the Judicial Police, and two people whose arrests were ruled lawful must do the same, Albanian Daily News reports, citing the court record. That's reported so far by one source. We're watching whether talks between students and the government begin despite Rama's renewed offer.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
